$comment: How the Taittirīya witnesses and commentaries line up with the edition's records (vallī.anuvāka). S is collated anuvāka by anuvāka; Madhva's text vallī by vallī (scope 'valli'), because it divides some anuvākas differently. 'analysed' lists the vallīs whose analysis is published and required by check.py (the others show the verified text, marked 'analysis in preparation').

notes.commentaries: Rāmānuja wrote no commentary on the Taittirīya. The Viśiṣṭādvaita commentaries are those of the six-commentary edition (Melkote): Kūranārāyaṇa, Raṅgarāmānuja (Prakāśikā), Bhāradvāja-Rāmānuja (Pratipadārthadīpikā), Rāmānanda (Ānandabhāṣya), Gopālānanda (Subodhinī, modern) and Kauśika Govindarāja. The edition prints several of them as running notes inside another commentator’s section, marked ‘आ.भा.’ (Rāmānanda), ‘तै. भा.’ (Govindarāja) and ‘प्र.’ (Raṅgarāmānuja), as its own colophons show; the importer files each passage under its commentator and cuts at the colophons. The source is OCR text and should be read against the printed book. Purāṇic and other verses that Madhva cites are reported as cited by him.
notes.corrections: The corrections restore readings that the base file has mistyped (spacing, a dropped or doubled letter); each is confirmed by the Sāyaṇa-pāṭha and by Madhva’s text, and none adopts a variant reading.
notes.rights: No modern translation was copied. The padaccheda, word tables, translations, explanations, commentary prose and studies are original to this edition, prepared for PaddySpeaks. Gopālānanda’s commentary is modern; only short quotations of it, with their locations, appear.

svara.label: Taittirīya Āraṇyaka, Sāyaṇa-pāṭha
svara.sources: Accents (svara) are shown on each anuvāka page only from the Sāyaṇa-pāṭha of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka, unit by unit, as keyed.
